messages:
Connor O'Brien: heads up, release train cutoff is tomorrow 2pm PT. need a decision on which quant PRs we’re taking vs punting. also need the exact checklist so we’re not debating it at the last minute.

Connor O'Brien: current candidates on my list:
- redwood#10621 (kernel-selection + quant-mode tracing spans)
- redwood#10622 (FP8 attention tuning H100/H200)
- redwood#10623 (INT8 GEMM conversion overhead / fuse dequant)
- redwood#10624 (scheduler batch-size cap override for quant decode)
- redwood#10625 (fix: auto-selector choosing FP16 for INT8 shapes)
- redwood#10627 (numeric drift checks FP8/INT8 vs FP16)
- redwood#10628 (KV cache: avoid redundant scale/zero-point conv)
- redwood#10630 (bugfix: FP8 prefill alignment long-context)
- redwood#10631 (structured perf log events)
- redwood#10633 (deprecate legacy INT8 toggle / consolidate flags)
- redwood#10634 (H200 tuning table behind capability detection)
- redwood#10635 (L40S fused-op revert / GPU-conditional disable)

Connor O'Brien: ask: which are safe to ship this train, and what tests are required for each? customer support flagged SUP-6193/SUP-6194 so I’m trying to avoid “quant changes” surprise landing without guardrails.

Sahana Iyer: +1 on nailing the checklist. from CI/gating POV, we can require:
1) unit + integration green (obv)
2) quant drift suite green (once 10627 lands) OR a one-off drift report attached for any kernels that change numerics
3) perf-canary green for 2 consecutive runs (nightly job) for quant modes on H100 + A100 (and L40S if we’re shipping L40S-specific change)
4) benchmark-lab e2e run for streaming scenario (TTFT/TPOT) on at least one GPU

Marissa Cole: release/canary workflow: I’m ok with landing behind a default-off knob if we can scope it to a cohort and have a one-click rollback. if it changes defaults, I want an explicit “quant defaults changed” section in the release notes + a pinned-config workaround.

Hiro Tanaka: kernel team POV:
- 10625 is a straight correctness fix (selector bug). should go in.
- 10630 is also correctness (alignment bug) and specifically addresses long-context FP8 prefill weirdness we saw. should go in if regression test is in.
- 10621/10631 are observability; low risk if guarded behind flag. recommend.

Hiro Tanaka: 10622 (FP8 attention tuning) is perf-only but touches launch configs. I’m comfortable shipping if:
- microbench delta is consistent (>= +3% tokens/sec on H100) and
- e2e TTFT doesn’t regress on streaming chat workload.

Grace Kim: for 10622 we already ran microbench on H100 and H200 perf lab nodes (once, not repeated). saw +5-8% kernel time improvement on the decode-heavy case. I can rerun with more reps today.

Yuki Sato: 10625 (selector bug) has a minimal guard + unit test for the shape. also improves logging in the selector path for attribution. I’ll add a quick note in the PR about which shapes were impacted.

Sofia Ivanova: scheduling side:
- 10624 adds a batch-size cap override for quantized decode. default is unchanged unless the config knob is set. risk is minimal.
- we do need to verify it doesn’t lower throughput too much under prefill-heavy workload. expectation: tail latency win, small throughput hit.

Noah Patel: I’m more nervous about 10623 + 10628 (INT8 GEMM conversion + KV cache conversion removal). those can change numerics and have weird corner cases. I’d prefer those ship only if 10627 drift gate is in the same release + we get a before/after drift summary on the “sensitive prompts” set.

Allison Grant: from observability: please ship 10621/10631. without those tags we’re blind in dashboards and can’t slice by chosen kernel/quant mode. it also helps postmortems when perf-canary screams.

release-bot: Reminder: Runtime Release Train R-2024.11.01 RC cutoff in 23h 12m. Please label PRs with `release-train-candidate` or `hold-next-train`.

Connor O'Brien: ok, proposing buckets:
SHIP THIS TRAIN (with checks):
A) redwood#10625 selector bugfix
B) redwood#10630 FP8 prefill alignment fix
C) redwood#10621 tracing spans (flagged)
D) redwood#10631 structured perf logs (flagged)
E) redwood#10633 flag consolidation (if it’s no behavior change)
F) redwood#10624 scheduler cap override (knob, default off)
G) redwood#10635 L40S conditional disable/revert (if it reduces correctness risk)

MAYBE (needs perf proof before cutoff):
H) redwood#10622 FP8 attention tuning (H100/H200)
I) redwood#10634 H200 tuning table (capability-gated)

HOLD NEXT TRAIN (unless someone convinces me today):
J) redwood#10623 INT8 GEMM fuse/dequant
K) redwood#10628 KV cache conversion removal
L) redwood#10627 drift checks (ironically: want it, but if it’s not stable by cutoff we can’t block the train)

Connor O'Brien: does anyone disagree?

Sahana Iyer: small tweak: I really want 10627 *in* the train even if 10623/10628 slip. it gives us guardrails for the next one + reduces rollback time for SUP-6194-type issues. unless it’s flaky.

Grace Kim: +1 ship 10627 if possible. we’ve been doing drift checks manually and it’s slow.

Noah Patel: agree with Sahana. 10627 itself is low risk (adds tests + gating policy) but could create noise if thresholds are too tight. if we ship it, make thresholds “warn” not “block” for the first week.

Marissa Cole: +1 on making drift gate warn-only initially. if it blocks the release train on day 1 we’ll hate ourselves.

Connor O'Brien: ok, updated: put 10627 in SHIP bucket if:
- it’s not flaky (3 consecutive CI runs green) and
- initial policy is warn/allowlist, not hard block.

Sahana Iyer: works. I can set it up as:
- CI job posts a comment + uploads drift artifact
- perf-canary remains the only hard gate for now

Sofia Ivanova: for 10624 (scheduler cap), my acceptance criteria for release:
- e2e streaming TTFT p95 no worse than +2% under mixed prompt lengths
- TPOT p95 improves or stays within noise
- ability to disable via config immediately

Connor O'Brien: can you provide exact config knob name + default value? want it in release notes.

Sofia Ivanova: knob is `scheduler.quant_decode_batch_cap`. default `null` (no cap). if set, it caps decode microbatch size only when quant mode != fp16. I’ll paste a snippet here once docs PR is up.

Allison Grant: for 10621/10631, please ensure tags include: `model_family`, `gpu_sku`, `quant_mode`, `kernel_id`, `phase=prefill|decode`. otherwise dashboard spec won’t line up.

Yuki Sato: 10621 emits `kernel_family` + `kernel_id` and `quant_mode` and includes shapes. I don’t think it includes `model_family` directly (that’s higher layer). but we can include model name in the span attributes where available.

Connor O'Brien: checklist (hard requirements) for SHIP bucket items:
- [ ] CI green (unit/integration)
- [ ] perf-canary: 2 consecutive passes on H100 quant job (and L40S if touching L40S)
- [ ] benchmark-lab e2e run attached for at least one top-hosted streaming workload (TTFT/TPOT + per-phase breakdown)
- [ ] drift report attached for any PR that changes numerics (or 10627 warn-only gate enabled)
- [ ] rollback plan: config pin or feature flag to disable (documented)
- [ ] release note entry: “Quantization / FP8/INT8” section with known caveats + workaround

Connor O'Brien: for MAYBE (10622/10634): also require microbench summary table + at least 3-run median delta.

Grace Kim: I’ll own the 10622 microbench reruns and post a short summary before EOD.

Hiro Tanaka: I’ll review 10622/10634 today and call out any risk (esp H200 path).

Marissa Cole: re SUP-6193: we should explicitly mention in notes “if you see INT8 latency regression, pin runtime to X or disable quant mode via config.” support will ask.

Connor O'Brien: yep. I’ll coordinate with support separately, but I’ll include a one-liner workaround in release notes.

Sahana Iyer: action items:
- I’ll update the release checklist doc + add labels on the PRs if you want.
- Connor: tell me which PRs are definitely in so I can wire gating expectations.

Connor O'Brien: definitive in (target): 10621, 10625, 10630, 10631, 10633, 10624 (knob), 10635, 10627 (if stable). 10622/10634 pending Grace/Hiro perf readout by tomorrow noon.

Connor O'Brien: if perf-canary fails on any of these, we drop the perf-only changes first (10622/10634/10624) and keep correctness + observability.

Marissa Cole: :thumbsup: (noted)

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: pls don’t drop observability 😅

Connor O'Brien: lol, observability stays.

release-bot: PR label audit: 3 PRs missing release labels: redwood#10622, redwood#10634, redwood#10627. Please update before EOD.
